name: Tselinny Center of Contemporary Culture
watch: Founder's wealth partly oil and gas; he was convicted and surrendered assets to the state.
why_flagged: Founder's wealth partly oil and gas; he was convicted and surrendered assets to the state.
records_note: Tselinny names its patrons by tier undated and lists an advisory board, but posts no annual report, accounts or governing board.

name: Turner Contemporary
watch: Dropped Stagecoach as Turner Prize sponsor in 2019.
why_flagged: Dropped Stagecoach as Turner Prize sponsor in 2019.
records_note: It files group accounts at Companies House for 2023 to 2025, names supporters by tier undated, and lists 15 trustees, but posts no reports.

name: UCCA Center for Contemporary Art
funding: Not-for-profit museum accredited by Beijing, funded by its gala, patrons, corporate sponsors and grants. 2025 partners: Louis Vuitton, Dior, Bloomberg and Aranya; 901,435 visitors.
watch: UCCA cancelled a 2019 Hung Liu show after Beijing denied a permit. In 2022 it pulled a Li Songsong painting after a complaint.
why_flagged: Not-for-profit museum accredited by Beijing, funded by its gala, patrons, corporate sponsors and grants. 2025 partners: Louis Vuitton, Dior, Bloomberg and Aranya; 901,435 visitors.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2024 and 2025, whose 2025 report names partners, and lists about 30 Foundation Council members; no accounts found.

name: Uzbekistan Art and Culture Development Foundation
funding: State foundation set up in 2017; runs the 2025 Bukhara Biennial.
watch: Bukhara Oil (Uzbekneftegaz refinery) is a partner; ACWA Power funded a prize show with Saudi Diriyah Biennale Foundation. Critics call it image-building.
why_flagged: Bukhara Oil (Uzbekneftegaz refinery) is a partner; ACWA Power funded a prize show with Saudi Diriyah Biennale Foundation. Critics call it image-building.
records_note: A state-run foundation under the Presidential Administration; its site names only its chairperson and posts no reports, accounts or donors.

name: V&A
records_note: It posts annual reports and accounts for 2011-12 to 2025-26, thanks named donors in the 2025-26 report, and names its trustees in each report.

name: Van Gogh Museum
records_note: It posts annual reports with a financial section (2024 on its own page), lists corporate patrons by name, and names its supervisory board.

name: Venice Biennale
funding: 2024 budget: public funds EUR 33.1M; tickets, sales and sponsorship 31.4M. 2026 donors include Getty, Ford, Batia and Idan Ofer and the Helis Foundation; Bvlgari and illycaffè are lead sponsors.
watch: The Helis Foundation, a 2026 donor, is funded by the Helis oil family. The EU ended a EUR 2M grant over Russia's pavilion in July 2026. In 2026 the jury resigned, artists withdrew from the awards and pavilions closed for a day.
why_flagged: 2024 budget: public funds EUR 33.1M; tickets, sales and sponsorship 31.4M. 2026 donors include Getty, Ford, Batia and Idan Ofer and the Helis Foundation; Bvlgari and illycaffè are lead sponsors.
records_note: It posts audited accounts for 2020 to 2025, names its board and auditors, and lists 2026 donors by name, but no separate annual report.

name: Victoria Gallery
watch: Sister institution of V-A-C ('Victoria — the Art of being Contemporary'); second site Victoria Underground since 2020.
why_flagged: Sister institution of V-A-C ('Victoria — the Art of being Contemporary'); second site Victoria Underground since 2020.
records_note: The gallery posts no annual report, accounts, partner list or board; its About page names founder Leonid Mikhelson and three managers.

name: Villa des Arts de Casablanca
watch: The founding and current funder is Al Mada, through its foundation. Al Mada owns 100% of Nareva, which holds 50.7% of the 1,386 MW Safi coal-fired power station. That makes a fossil-fuel (coal) owner the current and founding funder. No protest at the villa was found.
why_flagged: The founding and current funder is Al Mada, through its foundation. Al Mada owns 100% of Nareva, which holds 50.7% of the 1,386 MW Safi coal-fired power station. Nareva raised its stake by buying ENGIE shares in January 2025, and GEM reports Al Mada was set to take full control in October 2025. That makes a fossil-fuel (coal) owner the current and founding funder. No protest at the villa was found.
records_note: The villa's site sits behind a bot check and its Fondation Al Mada parent site did not load, so nothing could be checked.

name: Vincom Center for Contemporary Art
funding: Non-profit centre opened 2017, developed and financed entirely by Vingroup (property, retail, autos). Its own page dates from 2019.
watch: In 2025 Vingroup filed defamation suits against 68 people and organisations. No censorship at the centre found.
why_flagged: In 2025 Vingroup filed defamation suits against 68 people and organisations. No censorship at the centre found.
records_note: No records on its own site; parent Vingroup's reports could not be checked; partner logos are undated and no board names are shown.

name: VISUAL
watch: Civic center for contemporary art and performance in Carlow.
records_note: No annual reports; posts 2024 financial statements and a nine-member board with appointment years; funders appear as undated logos.

name: Vyksa Festival (Art-Ovrag)
